short: The most severe threat to English authority in Ireland during the Tudor period.
full:
Beginning in 1594, Hugh O'Neill, Earl of Tyrone, led a widespread Catholic rebellion against the advancing English administration in Ireland. Allied with Red Hugh O'Donnell, Tyrone built a highly organized and modernized Gaelic army, equipped with firearms and trained in continental tactics. The insurgency achieved several devastating victories against English forces, most notably at the Battle of the Yellow Ford in 1598, which destabilized English control outside the Pale and drew military support from Spain.

The conflict drained the English treasury, forcing Elizabeth I to commit over thirty thousand troops. The rebellion's turning point came at the Battle of Kinsale in 1601, where an English army under Lord Mountjoy decisively defeated a combined Irish-Spanish force. Mountjoy subsequently employed ruthless scorched-earth tactics, causing widespread famine across Ulster. Tyrone surrendered in March 1603, mere days after Elizabeth's death. The war destroyed the traditional Gaelic political order, paving the way for the plantation of Ulster under her Stuart successors.
